name: Alila Wuzhen
positioning: Contemporary Alila resort on the edge of the Wuzhen water town, with minimalist architecture inspired by a classic Jiangnan village and water flowing through the grounds
best_for: Travelers who want a calm, design-led base for exploring a Jiangnan water town
Guests interested in local crafts, tea and wellness experiences

facts.text: Alila Wuzhen is set on the edge of a water town, surrounded by winding canals, wooden corridors and stone bridges.
The resort is inspired by a classic Jiangnan village, reimagined with modern, minimalist architecture.
Accommodations include rooms and villas, such as the Garden Villa.
Spa Alila offers massages, facials and body scrubs, plus locally inspired treatments made with indigenous Wuzhen ingredients.
The 24-hour gym has dedicated yoga and meditation studios.
A tea experience with the resort's Tea Master includes tasting teas and painting with powdered tea leaves.
Wuzhen, in the Jiangnan region, is known as the 'Home of Silk' and is famed for its silk production.
Si Shui serves local cuisine with seafood from local lakes and ingredients from the resort's own farm, with a view of the central water feature.
The resort has an extensive whiskey collection.
Each guest room may accommodate up to two pet dogs.

highlights.text: Water flows through the resort, forming a water courtyard and wrapping around the suites and villas.
The resort's structures are situated around plantings of Metasequoia, an endangered native conifer.
The resort has heated indoor and outdoor pools with panoramic water views.
Guests can join a hands-on indigo dyeing workshop, working with master artisans to craft their own dyed creation.
A singing bowl sound journey combines a guided meditation with aromatherapy, and guests can play the bowls themselves.

considerations.text: The nearest listed airport is Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport, 82.4 kilometers away.
The hotel recommends local mapping apps such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map, as international mapping apps may not be accurate in Chinese Mainland.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires dedicated travel time.
